# Best RV Power Station + Solar Combos (2026)

The right pick depends on one question: **do you need to run the roof air conditioner?** A 13,500 BTU roof AC draws about 1,500 W running and spikes past 3,000 W at startup, so smaller stations can't start it. [emergencyenergy.co](https://www.emergencyenergy.co/articles/rv-power-station/)

## If you'll run the AC or boondock full-time

**EcoFlow DELTA Pro 3 is the best overall.**
- 4,096 Wh, expandable past 12 kWh
- 4,000 W continuous, 8,000 W surge
- Runs a roof AC for about 2.3 hrs, or a fridge, lights, laptop and Starlink for about 2 days
- Recharges 0–80% in about 50 min from a wall outlet
- Feeds the trailer's shore inlet through a TT-30 dogbone adapter
- Downsides: it takes two people to lift, and it's the priciest option once you add batteries
- [Review and price link](https://www.emergencyenergy.co/articles/rv-power-station/)

**Jackery Explorer 3000 Pro is the simpler choice for AC.**
- 3,024 Wh, 3,000 W continuous, 6,000 W surge
- Starts a 13,500 BTU AC without a soft-start kit
- [Source](https://www.emergencyenergy.co/articles/rv-power-station/)

**ALLPOWERS R4000 is the value pick with a direct buy link.**
- 3,456 Wh LiFePO4, 3,600 W continuous at 120 V, 6,000 W peak
- Has an RV outlet
- Takes 2,000 W of solar across 3 inputs, max 650 W each, 12–60 V
- 5-year warranty
- **Price:** $1,499. Code **EXTRA12** takes off $179.88, for **$1,319.12**. The code was tested 10/23 and expires 11/15. The store usually allows one code per order, and this one saves the most.
- Caveats:
  - It weighs 45 kg (about 99 lb), so treat it as a fixed install.
  - The "4,000 W" in the listing is the 230 V rating.
  - ALLPOWERS' refund page says sale items can't be returned.
- **Buy:** https://dealectric.com/go/allpowers-r4000-3456wh (affiliate link; the deal site earns a commission)

## Mid-range: no AC, but a fridge, lights, fans and electronics

**BLUETTI AC200L is the best value for RVs.**
- 2,048 Wh, 2,400 W continuous, 3,600 W surge
- Built-in 30A RV port
- **1,200 W solar input**, which is strong for a roof array
- About 62 lb
- [Source 1](https://www.emergencyenergy.co/articles/rv-power-station/), [Source 2](https://smartenergyedge.com/best-portable-power-station-with-solar-panels-for-camping/)
- Don't confuse it with the older **AC200P**, which some guides still recommend. The AC200P has only 700 W solar input, a 2-year warranty and slow 5–6 hr AC charging. [Source](https://outdoorpowerstations.com/articles/jackery-vs-ecoflow-vs-bluetti)

**EcoFlow Delta 2 Max** is another option in this tier. It's 2,048 Wh, charges 0–80% in 43 min from the wall, and expands to about 6 kWh. [Source](https://nomadsignal.co/blogs/news/jackery-vs-ecoflow-vs-bluetti-vanlife)

## Weekenders and light loads

**EcoFlow DELTA 3 Plus**
- 1,024 Wh, 1,800 W output, 1,000 W solar input across two 500 W inputs
- About 28 lb, expandable to 5 kWh
- [Source](https://smartenergyedge.com/best-portable-power-station-with-solar-panels-for-camping/)

The Jackery 1000 v2 is lighter at 23.8 lb, but its **400 W solar ceiling** limits how much panel you can use. [Same source](https://smartenergyedge.com/best-portable-power-station-with-solar-panels-for-camping/)

## Pairing the solar panels

- **Match the panels to the station's solar input limit.** A big roof array connected to a station with a low solar input wastes panel output. This is the most common mismatch in RV and van builds. [getwattlogic.com](https://getwattlogic.com/articles/bluetti-vs-jackery-vs-ecoflow-van-life)
- **A 300–400 W folding array refills a mid-size (about 2 kWh) unit in a full day of decent sun.** [Source](https://www.emergencyenergy.co/articles/rv-power-station/)
- **Same-brand panels make the connection simplest**, such as EcoFlow panels or Jackery SolarSaga. A Renogy 200W foldable suitcase is a common third-party choice. [Source](https://nomadsignal.co/blogs/news/jackery-vs-ecoflow-vs-bluetti-vanlife)
- **Stations with several solar inputs need panels on each input** to reach the full rating. That applies to the DELTA 3 Plus and the R4000.

## Quick picks
- **Running AC or living off-grid:** DELTA Pro 3, or the ALLPOWERS R4000 to save money
- **Most RVers:** BLUETTI AC200L with 400–800 W of panels
- **Weekends:** DELTA 3 Plus with 200–400 W of panels

Most of these sources are affiliate sites, and only the ALLPOWERS result included a direct store link. Confirm current prices and specs on the manufacturer's page before buying.

If you tell me your rig size, whether you need AC, and your budget, I can narrow this to one combo.
